questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^{2x}-1-2x}{x^2}$.
questions.explanation: Near $0$, $e^{u}=1+u+\frac{u^2}{2}+\dots$. With $u=2x$, the numerator is about $2x^2$. L'Hôpital twice gives the same value.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \pi/2}\frac{1-\sin x}{\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)^2}$.
questions.explanation: Put $t=\frac{\pi}{2}-x$. Then $\sin x=\cos t$, and $\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}\to\frac12$.

questions.text: Let $g(x)=\dfrac{x^2-4}{|x-2|}$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 2^+}g(x)-\lim_{x\to 2^-}g(x)$.
questions.explanation: $g=(x+2)\cdot\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}$. The right limit is $4$ and the left limit is $-4$.

questions.text: What is $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^-}\left(\frac1x-\frac{1}{|x|}\right)$?
questions.explanation: For $x<0$, $|x|=-x$, so the expression is $\frac2x$, which falls without bound. From the right it would be $0$.

questions.text: The graph shows $y=\dfrac{ax+b}{x-c}$ with asymptotes $x=2$ and $y=3$, passing through $(3,5)$. Find $a+b+c$.
questions.explanation: The vertical asymptote gives $c=2$, the horizontal one gives $a=3$. Through $(3,5)$: $\frac{9+b}{1}=5$, so $b=-4$.

questions.text: The graph of $y=\dfrac{3x}{\sqrt{x^2+4}}$ has two horizontal asymptotes. Find the distance between them.
questions.explanation: As $x\to\infty$, $y\to 3$. As $x\to-\infty$, $\sqrt{x^2}=-x$, so $y\to-3$. The distance is $6$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{x+a}-3}{x-5}$ for $x\ne 5$ and $f(5)=k$. If $f$ is continuous at $5$, find $a+k$.
questions.explanation: The numerator must vanish at $5$: $a=4$. With the conjugate, the limit is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}+3}=\frac16$, so $k=\frac16$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=x^2$ for $x\le c$ and $f(x)=2x+3$ for $x>c$. Find the sum of all values of $c$ that make $f$ continuous.
questions.explanation: We need $c^2=2c+3$, so $c=3$ or $c=-1$.

questions.text: Let $g(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor+\lfloor -x\rfloor$. Find $g(2)-\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 2}g(x)$.
questions.explanation: If $x$ is not an integer, $g(x)=-1$, so the limit is $-1$. At an integer, $g=0$. This is a removable discontinuity.

questions.text: The equation $x^3-2x-5=0$ has a root between the consecutive integers $n$ and $n+1$. Find $n$.
How many real solutions does $\sin x=\dfrac{x}{3}$ have?
questions.explanation: $x=0$ is one. For $x>0$: at $\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\sin x>\frac{x}{3}$, and at $\pi$ it's less, so there's one more. Beyond $x=3$ no solution is possible. By symmetry there is one for $x<0$.

questions.text: Apply the bisection method to $x^2-2=0$ on $[1,2]$. After three halvings, the root lies in an interval $[p,q]$. Find $p$.
questions.explanation: Midpoints: $1.5$ (too big), $1.25$ (too small), $1.375$ (too small). The interval becomes $[1.375,\,1.5]$.

questions.text: How many real roots does $x^5+x-1=0$ have?
questions.explanation: $f(0)=-1$ and $f(1)=1$ give one root. $f'(x)=5x^4+1>0$, so $f$ is increasing and can't cross zero twice.

questions.text: For how many integers $c$ does $x^3-3x+c=0$ have a root in the open interval $(0,1)$?
questions.explanation: $f'=3x^2-3<0$ on $(0,1)$, so $f$ decreases from $c$ to $c-2$. A root needs $c-2<0<c$, so only $c=1$ works.

questions.text: $f$ is differentiable with $f(1)=2$ and $f'(1)=3$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{f(x)^2-4}{x-1}$.
questions.explanation: This is the derivative of $f^2$ at $1$: $2f(1)f'(1)=12$.

questions.text: The line $y=3x+k$ is tangent to $y=x^3$. Find the product of all possible values of $k$.
The graph shows the derivative $f'$. Let $g(x)=x\,f'(x)$. Find $g'(1)$.
questions.explanation: $g'(x)=f'(x)+xf''(x)$. From the graph, $f'(1)=3$, and the slope of the line there gives $f''(1)=2$. So $g'(1)=3+2=5$.

questions.text: Let $y=\dfrac{(x+1)^3\sqrt{x+4}}{(x+2)^2}$. Use logarithmic differentiation to find $y'(0)$.
On the curve $x^2y+y^3=2$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $(1,1)$.
Let $y=\arctan(x^2)$. Find $y'(1)$.
Let $f(x)=x^5+x+1$ and let $g$ be its inverse. Find $g'(3)$.

collections.title: Calculus I · Limit Techniques
collections.description: Topics: factoring and conjugates; sin x / x and 1 − cos x limits; logarithm and exponential limits; sandwich theorem with floor functions; limits from a unit circle picture. 10 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · One-Sided Limits and Asymptotes
collections.description: Topics: limits read from a graph; one-sided limits with |x| and e^(1/x); composite limits such as f(−1 − t²); oblique asymptotes by long division; conjugates at infinity. 10 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Continuity and Discontinuities
collections.description: Topics: finding parameters at the joins; removing a discontinuity; telling holes, jumps and infinite breaks apart; floor functions; differentiability at a join. 10 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Intermediate Value Theorem
collections.description: Topics: locating roots by sign changes; counting real roots; bisection steps; fixed points and helper functions. 8 questions, 40 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Derivative by Definition and Tangents
collections.description: Topics: derivative from the limit definition; one-sided derivatives with |x|; functional equations; tangents from an outside point; curves sharing a tangent. 10 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Differentiation Rules and Chain Rule
collections.description: Topics: product and quotient rules from graphs; second derivatives; chain rule on composites; corners where a derivative fails. 11 questions, 55 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Implicit, Logarithmic and Inverse Derivatives
collections.description: Topics: implicit first and second derivatives; horizontal tangents on curves; logarithmic differentiation; derivatives of inverse functions. 8 questions, 40 minutes.
